$comment: Styling contract — layer 3: semantics. What each public name MEANS.
AUTHORED and versioned, never inferred. This is the layer the experiment
kept groping for in costumes — stba-description messages, token-meanings
json, the facet taxonomy — all of them kludges trying to record what the
The load-bearing field is 'not', not 'means'. A name's meaning is defined
by its edge: drift happens when an author needs a style that has no name,
stretches the nearest name past what it meant, and nobody can see that it
happened. 'means' alone cannot make that visible; 'not' + 'instead' can.
So every entry that has a plausible near-miss records it.
'was' records what a name is being collapsed FROM, where the census found
the old naming was actively wrong. It is migration intent, and it expires

page.means: The floor of the app — the colour you see where nothing has been placed.
page.use: The app/page background, behind everything else.
page.not: Anything raised or contained. If it holds content, it is a surface.
page.was: Collapses app-bg + body-bg, which differed by one step for no reason anything depended on.

surface.means: Raised content that sits ON the page — cards, dialogs, tables, panels.
surface.use: The default background for anything holding content.
surface.not: A sunken or alternating region inside a surface.

surface-alt.means: A sunken or alternate region INSIDE a surface — one step back from it.
surface-alt.use: Row stripes, wells, hover fills, sub-nav bars, code chips.
surface-alt.not: Muted TEXT. This is a background colour and always has been.
surface-alt.was: content-secondary — a misnomer the census caught: 88 of its 89 uses were bg-, and its values (#f8fafc light / #0f172a dark) are surfaces, not greys. It was never a text colour. Renamed, not collapsed.

text.use: Body copy, labels, headings, values — anything meant to be read first.

text-muted.means: Text that is present but deliberately de-emphasised.
text-muted.use: Hints, timestamps, counts, secondary detail, disabled labels.
text-muted.not: Input placeholder text — that is a form concern with its own contrast floor.
text-muted.was: content-muted (345 uses). Survived the grey collapse: it and text are the only two real text greys.

border.use: Card, table, input, and panel edges; dividers.
border.not: A focus ring — that is state, not structure.

accent.means: THE brand action colour. There is exactly one.
accent.use: Primary buttons, links, active tabs, focus, selected state — anywhere the brand asserts itself.
accent.not: Conveying success or failure. Accent means 'act here', not 'this went well'.
accent.was: Collapses primary + accent + brand. The census found a genuine split-brain: primary and accent were defined in two files with two different value sets (#3b82f6/#60a5fa vs #60a5fa/#38bdf8) and used 92 vs 26 times in templates — the same intent rendering two colours. Primary's values won on weight of use. 'secondary' is DROPPED: one consumer, dead utility classes, two conflicting definitions; gradients now carry their own stops.

accent-hover.use: Hover state of anything painted accent.
accent-hover.not: A second brand colour. It is one relationship away from accent and moves when accent moves.

on-accent.means: Whatever must stay legible ON TOP of accent.
on-accent.use: Label text and icons inside accent-filled controls.
on-accent.not: A text colour in its own right — it only exists in contact with accent.

link.means: Navigational text — this takes you somewhere.
link.not: A button that performs an action. Looking like a link is not being one.

focus.not: Selected or active state, which persist after focus leaves.

ok.means: It worked, or it is healthy.
ok.use: Success chips, healthy app state, passing checks.
ok.not: The affirmative button in a dialog — that is an action, not an outcome.

warn.means: Needs attention, but nothing is broken yet.
warn.use: Degraded state, approaching a limit, deprecation.

error.means: It failed, or it is broken.
error.use: Failure state, validation errors, error dialogs, destructive confirmation.
error.not: A destructive action that has not happened yet and might be routine.
error.was: Collapses danger + error, which were the same colour (#ef4444) under two names.

info.not: The brand action colour, despite sharing #3b82f6 today. They are the same value for now and may diverge — a brand may repaint accent without repainting info.

neutral.means: Unknown, not applicable, or not yet determined.
neutral.use: Tentative/unknown state, disabled or absent values.
neutral.not: A calm success. Unknown is not good news.

ok-soft.means: A background tint behind ok content.
ok-soft.use: Fill behind a success chip or banner.
ok-soft.not: Text or an icon — the tint has nowhere near text contrast.

warn-soft.means: A background tint behind warn content.
warn-soft.use: Fill behind a warning chip or banner.

error-soft.means: A background tint behind error content.
error-soft.use: Fill behind an error chip or banner.

info-soft.means: A background tint behind info content.
info-soft.use: Fill behind an info chip or banner.

neutral-soft.means: A background tint behind neutral content.

font-body.use: Everything not a heading and not code.

font-heading.use: Page and section titles. Defaults to font-body — a brand may split them.

font-code.use: Code, logs, CLI commands, raw values.
font-code.not: Anything chosen for looking technical rather than being code.

text-size.means: Base reading size. The whole type scale derives from it.
text-size.use: Set once per brand; density follows.

radius-control.means: Corner radius for things you click or type into.
radius-control.not: Cards and dialogs, which carry their own radius.

radius-surface.means: Corner radius for things that hold content.

spacing.means: The density knob. Tailwind v4's base unit — the entire spacing scale is a multiple of it.
spacing.use: Set once per brand to make the whole product tighter or looser.
spacing.not: A per-component nudge. Changing it moves everything, which is the point.

shell.means: The frame the app lives in — side nav, header, logo, page floor.
shell.note: Nav is the one region that is reliably inverted against the rest of the product, so it carries its own text and border colours rather than chaining to the globals.

page.means: Everything between the shell and the content — headers, breadcrumbs, tabs, sub-nav.

card.means: A bounded block of content on a page.
card.note: Cards and dialogs share a look today and differ in behaviour. Kept separate because a brand may well want a flat card and a raised dialog.

table.note: Row hover and stripe are the group's own; the stripe chains to surface-alt because a stripe IS a sunken region.

dialog.means: A surface that interrupts, with a backdrop.

popup.means: Transient overlays that do not interrupt — tooltips, snackbars, menus.
popup.note: The only group whose surface deliberately does NOT chain to the global surface: tooltips are inverted (dark on light) and inverting is the meaning, not a style choice.

form.means: Anything you type into, pick from, or toggle.
form.note: Placeholder is here rather than global because it has a contrast floor that muted text does not.

button.note: Carries only shape and weight — variant colours come from global accent and status. A button is not a colour; it is a shape with a colour applied by intent.

stepper.note: Its own group rather than folded into form or dialog: the rail and indicators are structure a form has no concept of.

status.means: State conveyed at a glance — chips, badges, indicators.
status.note: Carries only shape and weight. Colours come strictly from the global status set, so a state means the same thing everywhere it appears.

chart.note: The series palette is categorical: eight distinguishable hues carrying no meaning individually. Series-1 is not 'the good one'.

code.means: Monospaced literal content — editors, logs, CLI, raw values.
code.note: Syntax colours are deliberately NOT tokens. They come as a Monaco preset pair (light+dark) a brand picks, because a syntax theme is an internally-consistent set, not a bag of independent choices.

login.note: Its own group because it is the one surface an operator most wants to brand and the one place a user sees before any of the rest exists.

known_gaps.$comment: Recorded because an unrecorded gap is where drift starts.
known_gaps.per-group accent: Each group has --color-<group>-accent defaulting to the global accent. The census found ZERO consumers — nav-active is an alpha overlay, not a hue, and the one gradient is a background paint. 13 of the contract's 136 names exist on spec, not on evidence. They cost nothing while untouched (pure var() chain) but they are the contract's largest unproven surface.
known_gaps.gradients: Carry their own stops inline in group background values and may reference global accent directly. They do not depend on per-group accent. This is what replaced the dropped 'secondary'.
known_gaps.contract size: 136 public names against the draft's ~115 estimate. The gap is mostly per-group accent (13) plus per-group font/radius the draft counted loosely.
